title: UNIT 1: INTRODUCTION TO BIOLOGY
notes:
✓ Biology is the scientific study of life and living organisms.

It involves studying their structure, functions, reproduction, growth, evolution and interactions with the environment.

title: 1.1 Definition of Biology
notes:
✓ Biology is the branch of science concerned with the study of living organisms and their life processes.

Major branches include:
◆ Botany → study of plants.
◆ Zoology → study of animals.
◆ Microbiology → study of microorganisms.
◆ Ecology → study of organisms and their environment.
◆ Genetics → study of heredity and variation.

title: 1.2 Why Do We Study Biology?
notes:
Biology helps us understand living organisms and their relationships with the environment.

It is important for:
◆ Understanding health and diseases.
◆ Improving agriculture and food production.
◆ Conserving biodiversity.
◆ Developing medicines and biotechnology.
◆ Understanding environmental problems.
◆ Solving biological problems scientifically.

title: 1.3 The Scientific Method
notes:
✓ The scientific method is a systematic way of investigating questions and explaining natural phenomena.

Main steps:
1. Observation.
2. Question or problem.
3. Hypothesis.
4. Experiment.
5. Data collection.
6. Analysis.
7. Conclusion.
8. Communication of results.

title: 1.4 Tools of a Biologist
notes:
Biologists use laboratory and field tools to observe, measure, collect, prepare and analyze biological materials.

→ Laboratory tools → used for controlled experiments and specimen analysis.
→ Field tools → used for observing, measuring and collecting organisms or environmental data.

title: 1.4.1 Laboratory Tools of a Biologist
notes:
Common laboratory tools include:
◆ Flask → holds, mixes or heats liquids.
◆ Balance → measures mass.
◆ Dropper → transfers small amounts of liquid.
◆ Tongs → safely hold hot or small laboratory objects.
◆ Dissecting tool kit → contains tools for cutting, holding and examining specimens.
◆ Dissecting pan → supports specimens during dissection.
◆ Crucible → strongly heats small amounts of solid substances.
◆ Beaker → holds, mixes and heats liquids.
◆ Hotplate → heats substances without using a flame.
◆ pH meter → measures the pH of a solution.
◆ Thermometer → measures temperature.
◆ Spatula → transfers or handles small amounts of solid chemicals.

title: 1.4.2 Field Tools
notes:
Field tools are used outside the laboratory to observe, measure and collect biological specimens and environmental information.

Examples:
◆ Hand lens → magnifies small objects.
◆ Quadrat → samples organisms in a defined area.
◆ Sweep net → collects insects from vegetation.
◆ Measuring tape → measures distances.
◆ Binoculars → observe distant organisms.
◆ Specimen containers → safely collect and transport samples.

title: 1.5 The Light Microscope
notes:
✓ A light microscope uses visible light and glass lenses to magnify and resolve objects that are too small to see clearly with the naked eye.

It is commonly used to observe cells, tissues and microorganisms.

title: 1.5.1 Parts and Functions of the Light Microscope
notes:
◆ Eyepiece/ocular lens → magnifies the specimen for viewing.
◆ Objective lenses → provide different levels of magnification.
◆ Revolving nosepiece → holds and rotates objective lenses.
◆ Stage → supports the microscope slide.
◆ Stage clips → hold the slide in position.
◆ Diaphragm → controls the amount of light reaching the specimen.
◆ Light source/mirror → provides illumination.
◆ Coarse adjustment knob → provides rough focusing.
◆ Fine adjustment knob → provides precise focusing.
◆ Arm → supports the upper parts and helps carry the microscope.
◆ Base → supports the entire microscope.

title: 1.5.2 Magnification and Resolution
notes:
✓ Total magnification is calculated by:

Total magnification = Eyepiece magnification × Objective magnification.

Example:
10× eyepiece × 40× objective = 400×.

Magnification makes an object appear larger, while resolution is the ability to distinguish two close points as separate.

title: 1.5.3 Handling and Using a Light Microscope
notes:
1. Carry the microscope with two hands.
2. Place it on a stable surface.
3. Start with the lowest-power objective.
4. Place and secure the slide on the stage.
5. Use the coarse adjustment for initial focusing.
6. Use the fine adjustment for a sharp image.
7. Adjust the light and diaphragm.
8. Move to higher magnification only after obtaining a clear image.
9. Use fine adjustment at high power.
10. Clean lenses with lens paper and store the microscope properly.

title: 1.6 General Laboratory Safety Rules
notes:
✓ Laboratory safety prevents injuries, contamination and equipment damage.

◆ Wear a lab coat and appropriate eye protection.
◆ Tie back long hair.
◆ Never taste chemicals or specimens.
◆ Do not directly smell chemicals; use safe wafting when instructed.
◆ Handle glassware, chemicals and biological materials carefully.
◆ Keep the work area clean.
◆ Handle hot objects with appropriate tools.
◆ Follow instructions when using electrical equipment.
◆ Dispose of waste properly.
◆ Wash hands after laboratory work.
◆ Report accidents, spills and broken equipment immediately.
